newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader threatens parliament, court.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader threatens parliament, court.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko signed a decree on Thursday saying he would dissolve parliament and the constitutional court if they failed to abide by the result of a referendum the president hopes will back his bid for greater powers.

The decree, announced on state television by Lukashenko aide Mikhail Sazonov, countermanded decisions by the court and parliament, which ruled this week that the referendum scheduled for November 24 would not be legally binding.

"It (the decree) cancels, suspends the illegal decision of the Supreme Soviet (parliament) and the ruling of the constitutional court. From today they do not apply," Sazonov, first deputy head of the presidential administration, said.

"I am sure the parliament deputies are intelligent enough not to block the referendum...If anyone, any state body, interferes with the referendum, the activity of that body will be suspended," he added.

Parliament voted on Tuesday to uphold a court ruling made on Monday that only deputies could decide if the referendum -- which would extend Lukashenko's term by more than two years without new elections -- should have full constitutional force.
Lukashenko's decree seemed bound to cause an escalation in tensions between himself and a majority of deputies in parliament who have joined forces to oppose his increasingly authoritarian rule.
